title: Assessing Lysozyme-Like Activity in Galleria mellonella Hemolymph using EnzChek Kit
author: Juan Jose Quispe Haro
materials: All steps are done in the dark.

steps.title: Prepare Bacterial Suspension
steps.instruction: Prepare a standardized bacterial culture for injection.

substeps.instruction: Grow 3 ml of an overnight bacteria culture at 37 °C in an incubator with vigorous shaking (150-200 rpm).
Transfer 2 ml of the overnight bacterial culture into an Eppendorf tube.
Centrifuge at no more than 1000 rcf for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the bacterial pellet in 1 ml of sterile PBS.
Measure the absorbance at 600 nm and dilute the suspension to approximately 10^6 cells/ml.

steps.title: Inject Galleria mellonella Larvae
steps.instruction: Inoculate 7th instar larvae with bacterial suspension or control.

substeps.instruction: Select 7th instar Galleria mellonella larvae (usually >400 mg) and distribute in Petri dishes in groups of 5 per condition.
Prepare a Hamilton syringe with 10 µl of bacterial suspension or sterile PBS (for control).
Grab a larva by its sides, flip it upside down to expose the abdomen, and localize the hind/left proleg.
Carefully insert the syringe needle about 5 mm into the body and slowly inject the contents to prevent leaking.
Return the larva to its dish and repeat for all larvae and conditions.
Incubate the larvae in an incubator for 0-6 hours at 37 °C.

steps.title: Collect Hemolymph
steps.instruction: Extract hemolymph from larvae using sterile technique.

substeps.instruction: Surface sterilize micro scissors or scalpel blades by spraying with 70% ethanol and air drying.
Surface sterilize larvae by spraying them with 70% ethanol over a paper towel and air drying.
Optional: Anesthetize larvae on ice for 5-10 minutes to minimize movement.
Dispense 30 µl of anticoagulant buffer into 0.2 ml microfuge tubes (1 tube per larva) and register the mass of the tubes.
Make a small cut in the abdomen of the larva with the blade.
Gently squeeze the larva to collect 30-100 µl of dripping hemolymph into the pre-chilled tube containing 30 µl of ice-cold anticoagulant buffer (optional: use a 100 µl pipette for the last fraction).
Place the tube back on ice immediately after collection.
Register the weight and add ice-cold anticoagulant buffer to ensure a final hemolymph to buffer ratio of 1:1.
Repeat for all larvae.

steps.title: Process Hemolymph Samples
steps.instruction: Separate cellular debris and store the cell-free hemolymph (CFH).

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge tubes at a table top centrifuge at 12000 rpm for 1 minute (Optional: 4000 x g for 10 minutes at 4 °C).
Optional: Carefully transfer aliquots of the clear supernatant (CFH) to a new pre-chilled tube.
Optional: Snap-freeze aliquots in liquid nitrogen and store at -20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Lysozyme Standard Curve
steps.instruction: Create a series of lysozyme dilutions to generate a standard curve.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 8 microtubes with 50 µl of 1x reaction buffer.
Transfer tubes to an ice tray for a few minutes until ice-cold.
Add 50 µl of 1000 U/ml stock lysozyme to the first tube and mix by pipetting.
Perform 1:2 serial dilutions using the next 6 tubes; the 8th tube should contain reaction buffer only.
Optional: Flash freeze tubes in liquid nitrogen and store at -20 °C.

steps.title: Perform Fluorescence Assay
steps.instruction: Measure lysozyme-like activity using the EnzChek kit in the dark to avoid fluorescein conjugate formation.

substeps.instruction: In a black plastic 384-well plate, pipette 15 µl of the standard curve mixtures (and the buffer control) into three consecutive wells each.
Mix 25 µl of CFH with 25 µl of 1x reaction buffer and pipette 15 µl of this mixture into three consecutive wells of the plate.
Add 15 µl of 50 µg/ml DQ lysozyme substrate to each well (Note: one paragraph mentions 50 µl of substrate to 8 tubes, but the plate-specific step specifies 15 µl).
Cover the plate with a transparent lid or seal film, wrap in aluminum foil, and incubate at 37 °C for 30 minutes.
Measure fluorescence intensity with a top-reading microplate reader (Ex: 489 nm, Em: 523 nm).
Optional: Measure every 5 minutes for 30 minutes total to obtain an average read value.

steps.title: Analyze Results
steps.instruction: Calculate lysozyme activity based on the standard curve.

substeps.instruction: Pool the readings of each sample set and average the fluorescence intensity.
Generate a standard curve by averaging fluorescence readings per concentration and performing a linear regression.
Use the standard curve to calculate the lysozyme activity equivalent of the samples.
